title: Oxidation and Reduction
content:
# Oxidation and Reduction

## Learning Objectives

By the end of this lesson, you should be able to:
- Define oxidation and reduction in terms of oxygen
- Define oxidation and reduction in terms of electrons
- Identify oxidation and reduction in chemical reactions
- Explain why oxidation and reduction always occur together (redox)

## Introduction

**Oxidation** and **reduction** are fundamental chemical processes that always occur together. Understanding these reactions helps explain many important processes, from rusting to respiration to metal extraction.

## Key Concepts

### Definitions in Terms of Oxygen

**Oxidation:** Gain of oxygen
**Reduction:** Loss of oxygen

**Example:**
$$\text{2Mg} + \text{O}_2 \rightarrow \text{2MgO}$$
- Magnesium is **oxidised** (gains oxygen)

$$\text{CuO} + \text{H}_2 \rightarrow \text{Cu} + \text{H}_2\text{O}$$
- Copper oxide is **reduced** (loses oxygen)
- Hydrogen is **oxidised** (gains oxygen)

### Definitions in Terms of Electrons

**Oxidation:** Loss of electrons
**Reduction:** Gain of electrons

**Memory aid: OIL RIG**
- **O**xidation **I**s **L**oss (of electrons)
- **R**eduction **I**s **G**ain (of electrons)

**Alternative: LEO GER**
- **L**ose **E**lectrons = **O**xidation
- **G**ain **E**lectrons = **R**eduction

### Why Both Definitions Work

When magnesium reacts with oxygen:
- Mg atoms **lose electrons** → Mg²⁺ ions (oxidation)
- O atoms **gain electrons** → O²⁻ ions (reduction)

Losing electrons to oxygen is equivalent to gaining oxygen!

### Redox Reactions

Oxidation and reduction **always occur together**. When one substance is oxidised, another must be reduced.

These reactions are called **redox reactions** (reduction-oxidation).

**Example:**
$$\text{Zn} + \text{CuSO}_4 \rightarrow \text{ZnSO}_4 + \text{Cu}$$

In terms of electrons:
$$\text{Zn} \rightarrow \text{Zn}^{2+} + 2\text{e}^- \text{ (oxidation)}$$
$$\text{Cu}^{2+} + 2\text{e}^- \rightarrow \text{Cu} \text{ (reduction)}$$

- Zinc is **oxidised** (loses electrons)
- Copper ions are **reduced** (gain electrons)

### Oxidising and Reducing Agents

**Oxidising agent:** A substance that oxidises another substance
- It causes oxidation
- It is itself reduced (gains electrons)
- Example: Oxygen, chlorine, acids

**Reducing agent:** A substance that reduces another substance
- It causes reduction
- It is itself oxidised (loses electrons)
- Example: Carbon, hydrogen, reactive metals

## Worked Examples

**Example 1:** In the reaction below, identify what is oxidised and what is reduced.
$$\text{Fe}_2\text{O}_3 + \text{3CO} \rightarrow \text{2Fe} + \text{3CO}_2$$

**Solution:**
- Iron(III) oxide loses oxygen → **iron is reduced**
- Carbon monoxide gains oxygen → **carbon is oxidised**
- CO is the reducing agent
- Fe₂O₃ is the oxidising agent

---

**Example 2:** Identify the redox changes in:
$$\text{Mg} + \text{2HCl} \rightarrow \text{MgCl}_2 + \text{H}_2$$

**Solution:**
- Mg → Mg²⁺ + 2e⁻ (magnesium loses electrons, so is **oxidised**)
- 2H⁺ + 2e⁻ → H₂ (hydrogen ions gain electrons, so are **reduced**)
- This is a redox reaction

---

**Example 3:** In the thermite reaction, identify the oxidising and reducing agents.
$$\text{2Al} + \text{Fe}_2\text{O}_3 \rightarrow \text{2Fe} + \text{Al}_2\text{O}_3$$

**Solution:**
- Al is oxidised (loses electrons/gains oxygen) → **Al is the reducing agent**
- Fe₂O₃ is reduced (gains electrons/loses oxygen) → **Fe₂O₃ is the oxidising agent**

## Common Oxidation and Reduction Reactions

| Process | Type | Example |
|---------|------|----------|
| Combustion | Oxidation | CH₄ + 2O₂ → CO₂ + 2H₂O |
| Rusting | Oxidation | Fe + O₂ + H₂O → rust |
| Respiration | Oxidation | Glucose + O₂ → CO₂ + H₂O |
| Photosynthesis | Reduction | CO₂ + H₂O → glucose + O₂ |
| Metal extraction | Reduction | Fe₂O₃ + 3CO → 2Fe + 3CO₂ |
| Bleaching | Oxidation | Dye + oxidising agent → colourless |

## Summary Table

| | Oxidation | Reduction |
|---|-----------|------------|
| Oxygen | Gain | Loss |
| Electrons | Loss | Gain |
| Hydrogen | Loss | Gain |
| Happens to | Reducing agent | Oxidising agent |

## Common Mistakes

- **Mistake:** Confusing oxidation and reduction
- **Correct:** Use OIL RIG - Oxidation Is Loss, Reduction Is Gain (of electrons)

- **Mistake:** Thinking oxidation always involves oxygen
- **Correct:** Oxidation can also mean loss of electrons (even without oxygen)

- **Mistake:** Forgetting that both processes occur together
- **Correct:** If something is oxidised, something else must be reduced

## Practice Questions

1. Define oxidation in terms of (a) oxygen and (b) electrons. (2 marks)

2. In the reaction: 2Mg + O₂ → 2MgO
   a) What is oxidised? (1 mark)
   b) What is the oxidising agent? (1 mark)

3. Identify the substance oxidised and reduced in:
   CuO + C → Cu + CO (2 marks)

4. Write the half-equations for the reaction between zinc and copper sulfate solution. Label which shows oxidation and which shows reduction. (4 marks)

5. Explain why oxidation and reduction always occur together. (2 marks)

6. In the extraction of iron:
   Fe₂O₃ + 3CO → 2Fe + 3CO₂
   a) Identify the reducing agent. (1 mark)
   b) Explain why carbon monoxide is the reducing agent. (2 marks)

## Key Terms Glossary

| Term | Definition |
|------|------------|
| Oxidation | Gain of oxygen OR loss of electrons |
| Reduction | Loss of oxygen OR gain of electrons |
| Redox | A reaction involving both oxidation and reduction |
| Oxidising agent | A substance that oxidises another (and is itself reduced) |
| Reducing agent | A substance that reduces another (and is itself oxidised) |
| Half-equation | An equation showing either the oxidation or reduction part of a reaction |

## Summary

- **Oxidation:** gain of oxygen OR loss of electrons (OIL)
- **Reduction:** loss of oxygen OR gain of electrons (RIG)
- Oxidation and reduction always occur together (**redox**)
- **Oxidising agents** cause oxidation and are reduced themselves
- **Reducing agents** cause reduction and are oxidised themselves
- Many important reactions are redox: combustion, respiration, rusting, metal extraction
